checks: Re-read s110c_q20_templatefit.py and out/q20/s110c.txt, s110d.txt, s110e.txt and compared them with the three report.json entries (177 results). The quoted s, errors, ratios and upper limits match the outputs. I did not re-run the fits.

Method: the 4-3 wing map is fit as a*core+b+s_R*T_R+s_L*T_L at a common 4.5x3.0 arcsec beam. The templates are the 1.05 arcsec 3-2 excess (core-regression residual, as in s106a), and the error is max(OLS, shifted-template null sd, N=70 for the ridge). This is a sensible forward model given that Band 7 cannot separate the ridge from N (1.9 arcsec) and S (3.3 arcsec). The 3-2 fit recovers s=1.28+-0.43 (HCN) and 1.5+-0.6 (HCO+). The mirror controls are null, and the taper 1.5 vs 2.5 arcsec check agrees. I agree with this.

Significance is calibrated honestly. HCN 4-3 is 2.3 sigma, HCO+ 4-3 is 2.9 sigma, and the stack is 3.4 sigma. The report calls it 'weakly yes, ~3 sigma' and not a detection, which is correct. I would not let it be quoted as independent confirmation. The two lines share the template, the baseline treatment and the same pixels. The HCO+ 4-3 ridge Tb ratio of 1.3 is above the thermal limit, and the HCN 4-3 core coefficient is negative (-0.03). Both point to unmodelled systematics, so the stack error is probably underestimated.

Profile claim (ridge starts at ~200 km/s, lobe falls from the lowest |v|): the HCO+ lobe vs ridge centroid difference is ~2 sigma, and in HCN it is not distinguishable. The worker states this as mild support only. Agree.

Line ratios: r43/32 for the ridge and lobe agree within errors in HCN, and the HCO+ ridge/lobe ratio is 2.8 (+3.8/-1.4). HCN/HCO+ of the excess is ~1 in both places. The worker correctly concludes the pattern does not discriminate S counter-lobe from Bridge streaming. The Bridge alternative is excluded at only ~1.4 sigma. Agree. Not using the M18 1-0 scale is right.

Weak lines: CS 7-6, SO, HC3N and H13CN limits are 9-70x above the core line ratios. The SO/HC3N limits use the s106a-style 1 arcsec aperture null, with 267 control apertures. They are correctly called uninformative. The SO limit of <0.32 of the HCN excess is not a constraint on shocks. The H13CN s=-4.7 on the CO 3-2 tail is correctly not used.

fixes.what: Optional, for the publication text and the next round: add one template-free cross-check of the 3-2 vs 4-3 ridge excess. Convolve the Xb4d HCN/HCO+ 3-2 cubes to a beam that Xb47 can also reach (about 4.5x3.0 arcsec, or the Xb4f 5.7x3.5 arcsec products with Xb47 convolved up to match), and compare the ridge-position spectra of the 160-360 km/s window directly. Do the same for the lobe.
fixes.why: The only independent-line evidence rests on a fit that assumes the 4-3 excess has the 3-2 spatial shape. A direct matched-beam spectrum comparison, or the Xb4f-vs-Xb47 comparison, removes that assumption. It also tests whether the 3-2 ridge excess seen in Xb4f at 5.7x3.5 arcsec agrees with the Xb4d-derived one.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Smooth every cube to one beam. Take the beam spectrum at the position in question, subtract the nuclear core scaled from line-free positions, and compare the integrated wing in matched velocity windows with a noise null from a ring of control pixels.

fixes.what: Wording in the post. Say 'marginal ~3 sigma, template-dependent' and do not stack HCN and HCO+ as independent evidence. Make the headline 'no independent line test is possible with these data', not 'confirmed'.
fixes.why: Shared template and baseline systematics; the HCO+ 4-3 ridge is non-physical at 1 sigma.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Quote the per-line values with the shifted-template null error, and give the stack only as a consistency statement.

notes_for_questioner: The origin of the red ridge (S counter-lobe vs Bridge streaming) cannot be decided with these data. Line ratios, 4-3 excitation and the weak-line limits are all non-discriminating. What would decide it is a CO or JWST velocity-sign map beyond 250 pc, which is not in this dataset. Suggest closing the ridge origin as 'unresolved, data-limited' and moving on to the remaining open items. Possible new item: a 3-2/2-1 matched-beam ratio at the ridge using Xb55 (8.6x6.0 arcsec) vs smoothed Xb4d, tested only as a consistency check.
